subject: Clarification: evaluation cadence, fallback mapping & EU classification for ApexMed RFP
messages:
From: Alice Gonzalez <alice.gonzalez@apexmed.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@apexmed.com>, Dr. Samir Khare <samir.khare@apexmed.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ApexMed RFP — clarifications on governance + eval cadence

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP intake. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance and clinical teams so we can finalize scoring: 

1) NIST AI RMF mapping — can you supply a concise mapping (control-level) that shows which Redwood controls map to Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover? We need this for our risk committee. A spreadsheet is ideal.

2) EU AI Act classification — our legal team flagged that the intended use (clinical triage) might be high-risk in the EU. Can you outline how Redwood determines when a model or deployment is treated as high-risk vs. limited risk, and any deployment restrictions you recommend for EU-based patients?

3) Regression & evaluation cadence — we require a proposed cadence (automated + human-in-the-loop) and concrete triggers for rollback (metric deltas, hallucination rates, demographic performance drop). Please include example thresholds if you have them.

4) Evidence — please attach the SOC 2 report (if available), an example evaluation sampling plan, and any short notes on traceability between model versions and evaluations.

We attached our RFP questions as a PDF to make it easier to reference. Can we have the mapping and plan by COB next Wednesday (Apr 6)? If needed, happy to schedule a 30-minute session.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Gonzalez
Senior Procurement Manager
ApexMed Health

Attachment: apexmed_rfp_questions.pdf (pdf, 412 KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gonzalez <alice.gonzalez@apexmed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ApexMed RFP — clarifications on governance + eval cadence

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Answers and deliverables below; attaching the spreadsheet and the sampling plan for your team to review.

Short answers (high level):
- NIST AI RMF mapping: attached as redwood-nist-mapping.xlsx. We map controls to the RMF functions and include links to our operational docs (access, model lifecycle, monitoring, incident response). The sheet includes owners and evidence artifacts for each control.

- EU AI Act classification: Redwood evaluates use-case risk by combining (1) the declared intended purpose from the customer, (2) data subject population, and (3) the operation mode (fully automated vs. human-in-the-loop). For clinical triage we agree this is likely high-risk under the Act. Recommended posture: (a) prefer Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for EU patient data; (b) require human oversight for decisions impacting clinical pathways; (c) include tighter eval/regression cadence and shorter retention windows for model outputs. We include recommended contractual clauses in the SOW template.

- Regression & evaluation cadence (proposed):
  * Automated sampling: capture 0.5% of production requests daily (min 500 samples/day) and run automated regressions against the golden prompt set each night.
  * Human review: weekly human review of a random 1% sample and focused clinician review of any samples flagged by automated detectors.
  * Metric thresholds (example triggers):
    - F1 or task-specific accuracy drop > 2.0 percentage points vs. baseline over a rolling 7-day window -> create incident and pause rollout.
    - Increase in hallucination signal rate > 3x baseline or absolute > 1.5% (depending on task) -> immediate canary rollback.
    - Demographic performance variance > 5 percentage points between cohorts -> hold and escalate to governance board.
  * Canary rollout policy: staged rollouts (1% for 24 hours; 5% for 48 hours; 25% for 72 hours) with automated stop on threshold breach.

- Traceability & evidence: each served model version is associated with a single evaluation bundle (prompt set, metrics, artifacts). Our console stores model-version -> eval-id mapping and immutable artifacts; sample artifact names are in the mapping spreadsheet.

Attached: redwood-nist-mapping.xlsx, eval-sampling-plan.pdf, soc2-type2-stub.pdf.

Next steps: if that aligns, I'll consolidate a short one-page summary for your risk committee and propose language for the SOW. Want to do a 30-min walkthrough on Apr 5 at 10:00 AM PDT?

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-nist-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28 KB); eval-sampling-plan.pdf (pdf, 128 KB); soc2-type2-stub.pdf (pdf, 96 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ApexMed RFP — clarifications on governance + eval cadence

Eve — quick internal notes before we send final to ApexMed: 

1) Thresholds: suggest we make the hallucination threshold configurable per use-case; for clinical triage we might set absolute at 0.5% rather than 1.5%. Document this as a recommended safe default for high-risk medical tasks.

2) Adversarial / drift tests: add an automated adversarial perturbation job weekly (synthetic paraphrases + injection patterns) and include a drift detection alarm (KL divergence on embedding distributions).

3) Retention: recommend logs & traces for 90 days for operational debugging, with 365-day hashed index for auditability only (no raw content) unless customer requests otherwise.

4) EU deployment note: include explicit gating that EU high-risk deployments require on-prem or VPC + KMS-managed keys and optional HSM for signing audit trails.

I'll review the draft one-pager you promised. If we're aligned I'll sign off and ask Marissa to attach the SOW redlines.

- Karthik

Subject: Consolidated response + materials for ApexMed RFP — proposed review call Apr 6

Hi Alice/Team —

Thanks for the questions and for letting us iterate. Attached are the deliverables:
- redwood-nist-mapping.xlsx — control-level mapping to NIST AI RMF with owners and evidence pointers.
- eval-sampling-plan.pdf — nightly automated cadence and weekly human-in-the-loop review process.
- soc2-type2-stub.pdf — stub indicating SOC 2 Type II coverage; full report available under NDA (we can share with your legal team).

Key consolidated points:
- Classification: clinical triage is treated as high-risk. We recommend Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for EU-hosted patient data, required human oversight, and HSM/KMS-managed keys as per your compliance team.
- Regression cadence & triggers: automated daily regressions (0.5% sample min 500/day), weekly human review (1% sample), with example triggers and a staged canary (1%/24h -> 5%/48h -> 25%/72h). Per Karthik's feedback we will expose the hallucination threshold as a configurable parameter and include adversarial perturbation tests in the weekly pipeline.
- Traceability: each model version will be linked to an immutable evaluation bundle; we provide artifact ids in the mapping sheet.
- Retention: operational logs 90 days (raw), 365-day hashed index for audit; option to extend per contract.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-minute walkthrough of the mapping and sampling plan — suggest Apr 6 at 10:00 AM PDT (invite attached).
2) If acceptable, we will add the recommended governance clauses into the SOW and provide the SOC 2 under NDA.

Action: please confirm the call time or propose alternatives. We'll also send a short one-pager for your risk committee before the call.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
